what: judo.sh generate-root failed with a Maven daemon connect timeout because the mvnd registry file was corrupt.
why: Corrupt ~/.m2/mvnd/registry/1.0.2/registry.bin (Bad string size). Local tooling state, not a catalog topic.
workaround: Killed mvnd processes, deleted registry.bin, reran generate-root.
note: Session L66-69 shows the mvnd registry.bin error; it is a corrupt local file, not a platform defect. At most one troubleshooting line (kill mvnd, delete ~/.m2/mvnd/registry/*/registry.bin) in catalog/agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md; catalog only mentions mvnd as optional in integration-testing/README.md.

what: managed=true on an actor principal is meant to insert the principal row at first login, but the runtime does not do this. An AuthenticationInterceptor is needed.
why: The advanced-modeling pattern doc warns that auto-insert is not implemented in the current runtime, and the JIT best-practice confirms it.
workaround: Builder set managed=false and planned the row differently (see c01-11 and c01-45).
note: Catalog already states the runtime gap at lines 55 and 76 (DefaultActorResolver only looks up, managed insert not implemented) and has keycloak-jit-user-provisioning. Nothing to add.

what: A Keycloak user and the application's actor row are two separate stores. The runtime needs both before it can resolve the actor.
why: Stated by the builder in its seed script header. Matches the catalog's Keycloak Users and the Entity Store section.
note: Keycloak user vs entity-store row is documented (also judo-doc-problems.md record on managed user sync). Nothing to add.

what: After the generated table was patched and listed in .generator-ignore, ./judo.sh build -f failed with 'manual changes' on many generated frontend files (App.tsx, auth files, components). Only build -f -i passed.
why: Generator checksum check is not satisfied by the module .generator-ignore entry, so every changed or unlisted generated file blocks the frontend build. -i disables the check and refreshes checksums, which also hides real manual edits.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh build -f -i, later ./judo.sh build -M -B -i.
note: Catalog documents -i (build-process.md:221) and .generator-ignore (custom-public-assets.md:28) but nothing on the false positive where the frontend build reformats generated files after checksum capture, which is what hit App.tsx and auth files; judo-doc-problems.md already lists this. Session L423-427 is the symptom, not a root cause in judo-ng.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md or frontend/build-and-deployment.md: "A second build can fail with manual changes on untouched files (Biome reformats after checksum capture); use build -i; .generator-ignore does not cover these."

what: After a frontend-only rebuild, Karaf still served the old frontend bundle from application/.karaf/system. The builder had to delete application/.karaf and restart.
why: Unpacked Karaf assembly was not refreshed by build -f; the old jar stayed in .karaf/system.
workaround: rm -rf application/.karaf, then build -i and start.
note: Session L557-569 shows the old asset index served until application/.karaf was removed and the cause is the Karaf system repo caching the SNAPSHOT jar; judo.sh uses KARAF_DIR=${APP_DIR}/.karaf (L925). Likely stale-SNAPSHOT behaviour rather than a distinct bug; cause not proven.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/development-workflow.md: "After a frontend-only rebuild, stop, rm -rf application/.karaf and start if the old bundle is still served."

what: Karaf log after a restart showed NoClassDefFoundError for EolExecutionContext in the RDBMS OSGi bundle.
why: Unknown; the builder saw it and did not pursue it. Login and data still worked.
note: One NoClassDefFoundError line at L621 (EolExecutionContext not found by rdbms bundle) at a restart; no reproduction, no recurrence, and the app started. Possibly an OSGi start-order race. Not enough for a ticket.

what: Karaf startup prints 'Visit http://localhost:8181/api-spec/webshop', but that URL returns 404.
why: Startup log link does not match the served API spec path (the REST root is under /api/).
workaround: Used REST paths from the generated frontend services.
note: Banner prints http://localhost:8181/api-spec/webshop (ApplicationListener.java:224) and session L476-477 shows 404 for that exact URL. Catalog deployment/README.md:161 and osgi-runtime-services.md:103 promise the same URL; trailing slash or later servlet registration not tested.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/osgi-runtime-services.md: note that /api-spec/<model> returned 404 in the webshop run (verify), use generated frontend REST paths.

what: Build log showed ERROR lines for com.sun:tools systemPath ${tools.jar} but BUILD SUCCESS was reported.
why: Generated pom uses a relative system path for tools.jar. Noise, not a failure.
note: Log lines at L155-156 show the systemPath ${tools.jar} ERROR next to BUILD SUCCESS; I found no tools.jar reference in the judo-ng XML I searched, so the source is a dependency pom (not located). Cosmetic noise.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md: "com.sun:tools systemPath errors in the Maven log are harmless when BUILD SUCCESS is printed."

what: Setting customImplementation=true on the ProductInfo_Table price element makes the generated table component use useTrackService without importing it. The frontend build fails with TS2304 'Cannot find name useTrackService'.
why: Generator bug in the table component template for custom-implementation columns. The build recovery section (delete generated src folders and rebuild) did not fix it.
workaround: Set customImplementation=false on the table price element, regenerated, and built. The price column is handled by the column customizer hook instead.
note: Session L962-970 shows TS2304 after customImplementation=true on a table column. In judo-ng the template line 190 of containers/components/table/index.tsx.hbs calls useTrackService; the import condition for that file was not checked, so the bug is plausible but not pinned.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/hooks/table-hooks.md: do not set customImplementation=true on table columns; use ColumnCustomizerHook.

what: The generated table component builds the column customizer lookup filter with a missing closing parenthesis after (column=price), so the OSGi filter is invalid.
why: Generator bug in the table component template for customizer lookups; found when customImplementation was enabled on the table column.
workaround: Not patched (generated file). Table column left generated; logged in GAPS R1-1.
note: The filter string "(&(${OBJECTCLASS}=...)(component=...)(column=name)" opens "(&" and never closes it, so the OSGi filter is invalid. Real defect, reproducible by reading the template.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/hooks/table-hooks.md: warn that ColumnCustomizerHook lookup is broken in the generated table template (version-specific, verify).

what: Field reorder did not reach the generated form and view. After move, relocate and row changes, the saved model showed Name, Price, Description, but the generated TSX and the generated UI model still listed price first, then name, then description. Orchestrator first reported the symptom in Round 2 (Price above Name on the details page).
why: Root cause given by the orchestrator in Round 4: the esm2ui ETL emits widgets per type in rule order, so number widgets come before text widgets; model order and row are ignored (see c02-55).
workaround: Pending; the builder tried delete and re-fill and update --add feature, see c02-49.
note: Field order bug is the same root cause as c02-46: __pos.put(self, __pos.get(component) ?: 0) at visualElement.eol:5. Model order is ignored for generated forms and views. Merged with the other field order claims.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/esm-to-ui-mappings/README.md: "Generated field order follows widget rule order, not model order; number fields appear before text fields; do not rely on move/relocate."

what: Frontend build failed once (pnpm run build error) after the fields were deleted and the priceLabel removed. The next build passed after a regenerate, with no change in the cause shown.
why: Not diagnosed in the chunk; the failed build log line only shows the pnpm exec error. Possible cause: deleted fields still referenced by the custom implementation registration.
workaround: Re-ran generate and build; the second run passed.
note: One failed build then a pass after regenerate with no cause visible; typical stale generated state. Nothing actionable.

what: The shipped esm2ui transformation is a compiled Java 'zeta' package without readable rules, so the builder could not see the exact rule that orders generated fields. Only the older ETL source was readable.
why: Shipped tatami esm2ui jar contains compiled classes for the current version; the readable ETL is from an older jar.
workaround: Logged in GAPS R3-1 as open; field order tests kept red.
note: Same field-order problem; the ZETA vs ETL split is already in model-validation-and-transformation.md:19. Readable rule source is only in judo-ng (visualElement.eol). Merged into c02-40.

what: Root cause of the field order bug (orchestrator, Round 5): esmToUi.etl sorts container children by ESM position (pre block ~line 77, post block ~line 114), but operations/ui/visualElement.eol:5 looks the position up with __pos.get(component) ?: 0. For these fields the lookup misses, so every position is 0 and the stable sort keeps rule-firing order, so number widgets come first. Groups inherit the order from their first child's rule.
why: Platform bug in the esm2ui transformation (judo-tatami-esm2ui, ETL position lookup). Earlier the orchestrator also cited dataField.etl rule order (Round 4) as the mechanism.
workaround: No workaround yet: Group wrappers tried in Round 4 did not change the order. Round 5: wrappers removed; the two field-order tests marked test.fail() with a comment naming the bug.
note: Confirmed in judo-ng: line 5 is `__pos.put(self, __pos.get(component) ?: 0);`. This is the root cause for the field order group. (The jsl2ui counterpart visibleDeclaration.eol:11 handles missing positions differently.)

what: Maven validate and build print systemPath errors for com.sun:tools (tools.jar not absolute) in the generated build log, on every build; BUILD SUCCESS is still printed.
why: Generated pom uses a relative tools.jar path; the build still reported BUILD SUCCESS.
workaround: Noted only; build succeeded.
note: Same tools.jar noise as c01-44 seen again in logs L1801, L2122.

what: Admin details page shows Price before Name and Description; the field order test failed, so the builder marked it test.fail() with a reason.
why: Generated view orders the number widget before the text widgets; same platform bug as the create form.
workaround: test.fail() with reason; the customer front has its own details layout that fixes the order.
note: Same field-order symptom on the details page; test.fail() workaround is a project choice.

what: Admin product view cannot show the stored image: the generated binary field is an upload control that shows the file name, so the image test on the admin view was changed to check the file name.
why: The generated admin binary widget is an upload field; a picture view needs a custom display, which the customer front provides.
workaround: Admin test asserts the file name; the customer front shows the image through the generated ImageDisplay path.
note: The generated admin binary field is an upload control showing the file name; this is design behaviour, not a bug. Catalog should say that an image preview needs a custom visual element (see binary-blob-url-hook.md).

what: Customer addresses list via CustomerAccount!filter(...)!any().addresses showed only 2 of 6 stored addresses.
why: Cause not found in one kb-guided try; the !any() form on the composed list returned a partial list.
workaround: Replaced with Address!filter(a | a!container(CustomerAccount).email == ...) from the container back-reference pattern; the list then showed all addresses.
note: `CustomerAccount!filter(...)!any().addresses` returns the addresses of ONE account by definition, so 2 of 6 (other addresses belong to other customers) is expected, not a platform bug. The back-reference form is the correct pattern and is covered. Evidence L2306-2316 shows a missing gridcell, not a count mismatch.

what: Keycloak first-login row insert is not done by the runtime for the managed customer actor, so custom Java was needed.
why: Documented runtime limit: managed actor auto-insert is not implemented in the current runtime.
workaround: CustomerProvisioningInterceptor in application/interceptors.
note: Same as c01-09; JIT provisioning is covered by best-practices/backend/keycloak-jit-user-provisioning.md.

what: Renaming the customer product transfer object forced hand edits of custom frontend files (renamed custom-implementation file, new constants, container and type paths) and deletion of stale generated customer folders.
why: Custom frontend file names and constants are derived from the transfer object name; stale generated containers stay behind after a model change. The builder found the recovery steps in build-process.md.
workaround: git mv of the custom file, search-and-replace of names and paths, removal of generated pages, dialogs, containers and services folders, then regenerate.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md (renaming a transfer object: which generated and custom files follow)
note: Builder found Frontend Build Recovery in build-process.md. Missing: renaming a TO renames custom-implementation files and constants. Add one line: "After renaming a TO, rename custom files/constants and delete stale generated pages/dialogs/containers/services before regenerating."

what: Running pnpm format by hand failed because the lockfile entries were newer than the minimumReleaseAge policy.
why: pnpm policy in the generated frontend rejects lockfile entries published within the cutoff; the real build failure was the duplicate import (c04-13), so this was a side issue in the investigation.
proposed_target: generated frontend pnpm configuration (minimumReleaseAge vs lockfile)
note: pnpm minimumReleaseAge vs lockfile is a local pnpm policy conflict (L2468-2471), not JUDO behaviour. One-off.

what: An operation with an output and an input dialog makes the generated dialog file import the output type twice (import type { OrderInfo, OrderInfo, ... }); Biome rejects it as a parse error and the frontend build stops.
why: Generator bug. Tried mapped output, output with a relation to the same type, and output with one primitive: all failed the same way. The catalog's operation-return-type-navigation pattern (return the destination type from the operation output) is therefore blocked.
workaround: Made checkout a void operation; the new order is opened through the generated dialog actions hook (see c04-14).
proposed_target: generator: dialog types for operations whose output is also a post-call navigation target
note: Session L2475 shows `import type { OrderInfo, OrderInfo, OrderInfoStored, OrderInfoStored }` and Biome parse error "second declaration of OrderInfo". Reproducible build error; template file not pinned in judo-ng.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/best-practices/model/operation-return-type-navigation.md: warn that an operation with both an input and an output of the same TO breaks the frontend build (verify version).

what: A business fault shows in the generated fault dialog as the error code letter by letter (0: N, 1: O, 2: T ...), not as a readable message.
why: The generated 422 handler opens the dialog from the first key of the response body; the body starts with 'code', not the fault. The catalog describes the body with the fault key first, which is wrong for this version.
workaround: Error handler interceptor shows the fault's message as a snackbar (documented route in the frontend error-handling page).
proposed_target: generated error-handling.ts (422 handler takes first key); catalog body order in error-handling.md
note: Catalog frontend/error-handling.md already states the handler uses Object.keys(data)[0]; the symptom (letters) fits a body whose first key is `code`. So catalog is incomplete on the body shape, not simply wrong. Session L2372-2373.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/backend/error-handling-guide.md and frontend/error-handling.md: show the actual 422 body (first key) and recommend the error handler interceptor.

what: Menu order is not taken from the model: the drawer shows Products, My orders, My addresses, Cart, My profile although the model lists Cart second; move commands had no effect on the generated order.
why: Menu order is decided by the generated drawer; the builder did not use the menu customizer hook.
note: Menu order not following model matches ui-hooks.md Reordering Menu Items (hook is the route) and the field-order family. Already documented.

what: After a successful removeProduct, the generated page says the operation succeeded, refreshes the deleted product (404 BOUND_OPERATION_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND) and never opens the output dialog.
why: Generated post-operation flow refreshes the bound instance after an operation that deletes it.
workaround: Page actions hook registerProductRemovedHook.ts (documented postRemoveProductForProductInfoAction): shows the returned message and goes back to the product list.
proposed_target: generated admin page flow for operations that delete the bound instance
target: judo-ui-react-template page actions after delete operation
note: Generated flow refreshes the deleted instance (BOUND_OPERATION_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND). Plausible and documented hook workaround exists; template not pinned in judo-ng.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/hooks/action-hooks.md: for instance operations that delete the instance, add a post-action hook that navigates back.

what: Existing Postgres volume was not migrated after the model added SalesOrderLine.product: queries failed with column c_product_id does not exist. ./judo.sh schema-upgrade then failed (SCHEMA_DIR empty, Maven cannot read the schema project), so the containers and both volumes were wiped and re-seeded; this repeats the R6-1 gap for the third round.
why: Generated judo.sh schema-upgrade path bug; the catalog says a development database needs no step, which does not hold for an existing volume with data.
workaround: Wipe containers and volumes, restart, scripts/seed-dev-user.sh, seed tests (repeated in R10 with the same failure).
note: judo-ng judo.sh line 991: SCHEMA_DIR=${schema_dir:-$MODEL_DIR}, so the schema POM path is wrong unless schema_dir=application is set; this is a template default and the catalog has no mention of schema_dir. Catalog also claims no step is needed for a dev database, which fails for a persistent volume (L2921).

what: A plain ./judo.sh build after generate failed with There are manual changes in the generated files (frontend files reformatted), although git showed no change; the build passed with -i.
why: Frontend build reformats generated files and the generator then treats them as hand-edited; cause not found by the builder.
workaround: ./judo.sh build -i (the checksum-mismatch option from agent-docs/frontend/README.md).
proposed_target: frontend build checksum handling after generate
note: Same as c01-20 (judo-doc-problems.md already records the Biome reformat false positive).

what: Model-built label strings (for example the order total label and line labels) stay in English with EUR format in Hungarian, because model expressions cannot pick the UI language.
why: Derived string members are fixed text; the Price component is the only locale-aware formatter.
workaround: Left as is; logged. Customer cart and shop use the Price component.
note: Model expressions have no UI language; derived strings stay in one language. Catalog should state "format display strings in the frontend, not in derived model strings". This is a design limit, not a ticket.

what: After Apply coupon or Remove coupon the generated cart page does not give the custom cart summary component new data, so the total stayed stale.
why: Post-operation flow does not refresh custom visual components.
workaround: Post-operation hooks dispatch a window event; the cart component listens and reloads; cart component also reloads on new signed identifier.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/hooks/action-hooks.md (refresh of custom components after an operation)
note: Custom visual components are not refreshed after operations; window event workaround is the builder pattern. Add the recipe; not enough to call it a bug.

what: Admin build log shows XMI ID COLLISION DETECTED errors (ten lines) for the e2e and frontend model; the build still succeeds.
why: Cause not investigated by the builder.
workaround: Ignored; logged.
proposed_target: generator XMI id reassignment for admin actions
note: XMI ID COLLISION lines at L3145-3147 with BUILD success. I found no such string in judo-ng java/etl, so the source was not located. Cosmetic.

what: Field order on the order views: new fields are appended, so Total sits before Ship to and Coupon last on the admin order view.
why: Known generator family (R3-1): field order follows rule firing order, not the model.
workaround: move used for Ordered only; not tidied.
note: Field order family.

what: The same timestamp is shown in two time zones: Ordered reads 02:03 while history rows of the same order read 03:03.
why: Model and browser time zone handling differ from the JVM zone used in custom Java.
workaround: None; logged as open.
proposed_target: defaultZoneId versus browser zone for timestamps
note: Known: platform-behavior-reference has a Time and Time Zones section, audit-event-trail.md:29 and judo-doc-problems.md already record the UTC vs browser zone split. The builder consulted it (L3236-3238). Not a new ticket.

what: Browser tests cannot set the business clock: WEBSHOP_BUSINESS_DATE is read once at class load, so it needs an application restart.
why: Catalog documents a start-up override for the injectable clock; no way to set it per test was found.
workaround: Tests use real dates around today (expired is yesterday, not yet valid is in two days).
note: The clock pattern is in the catalog; a static final read at class load needs restart is a project design choice. Note a one-liner in that page is optional.

what: Sale price window uses Date!now() in the model, so it follows the platform clock, not the business clock used by custom Java.
why: Model expressions cannot call the Java clock; the catalog says so.
workaround: Window tests use dates around today; the cart and order read the derived effectivePrice, so display, cart and order agree.
note: Builder says the catalog states model expressions cannot call the Java clock; platform-behavior-reference covers Timestamp!now().

what: Transform failed on a derived attribute that filters over a two-way collection (Product.wishedBy): 'Feature wishedBy not found', then an ObjectFilterExpression cannot be cast to CollectionExpression error in asm2expression.
why: Not explained in the chunk; occurred when a derived flag filtered the reverse side of a many-to-many two-way relation.
workaround: Set wishedBy cardinality to 0..* and re-created the derived flag with a different expression; some derived flags were removed and rebuilt.
note: Session L3376-3381 reproduces two errors: "Feature wishedBy not found" and ObjectFilterExpression cannot be cast to CollectionExpression, resolved only by changing cardinality to 0..*. Exact source cast not located in judo-ng; first error is probably a transient state during rename.
also: modify-catalog: catalog/best-practices/model/bidirectional-relation.md: filtering the reverse side of a two-way relation needs upper cardinality set to * before using it in a derived filter (verify).
